checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The prose is meticulous and controlled — the hum, the worn handholds outside 5-C, the commons wall's repainted numbers — but these textures are deployed as thematic reinforcement of the ledger-and-loss structure rather than as seductive, strange-beautiful sensory hooks; the piece opens with dry procedural exposition (stress readings, coherence decay curves, wrist displays) and stays in that register throughout, so allure never precedes or exceeds the accurate observation.
checks.Fix: Open with a sustained, sensory immersion in Candelaria's specific wrongness-made-beautiful (the sound of a bloc breathing, the smell of sixty-year-old recycled air, the vertiginous view through the outer ring) before pivoting to Teo's clinical readings, so the reader falls in love with the place before the ledger starts subtracting from it.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening beats — Teo checking stress readings on the gantry, the commons wall ritual of repainting the altitude number, the walk deck-by-deck through worn handholds and the machine shop sign — establish the world's ordinary texture (the Hush, freeboard, Air Tax) entirely through a character who has stopped being surprised by any of it, before the AshgraveMaterials letter introduces plot pressure.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'the Hush' (coherence drivers holding the bloc aloft), 'The Low' (no governance line, no Air Tax bracket, salvage waiting for a claimant), 'Air Tax' (a fee on altitude explained in one clause), and 'freeboard' (glossed via the surface-hull analogy 'back when hulls floated on water') are each folded into Teo's working thoughts as she'd actually think them, oriented at first use without stopping the narrative to explain.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: The story is scrupulous about most in-universe jargon (e.g. 'Air Tax,' 'freeboard,' 'certified salvage' are all glossed), but the currency symbol 'Φ' is used from its very first appearance ('Total offer: Φ847,000') with no explanation of what it stands for or how to read it, and 'NSB'-style acronyms are otherwise avoided entirely, suggesting the rule was followed for true acronyms but the symbol itself was never glossed.
checks.Fix: Add a brief in-voice gloss the first time Φ appears, e.g. having Teo mentally note 'Φ — Phos, the city's standard currency mark' before or as she reads the AshgraveMaterials letter.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The clearest human crack for Teo is the tether-platform photograph 'propped against the wall where it always sat, never hung — because hanging it would have meant deciding it belonged somewhere permanent, and she still wasn't sure it did,' paired with her fifty-one-kilo life and the realization that her own lightness kept her from understanding what weight costs others until Prita's hand pressed to her sternum.
checks.Fix: Let that photograph beat breathe a moment longer with a concrete sensory or memory detail (what's in the photo, who's in it) rather than only abstracting it into the 'permanence' theme, so the crack lands as a felt image instead of another analytical observation.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The final image—Candelaria touching down after the Hum goes quiet—is a genuine 'one beat past the handoff' gesture, but it lands as resolution rather than residue: the plot's central tension (will it sell, will it survive) is fully closed, and the descent is rendered as clean, almost peaceful ('exactly the way a healthy descent should sound'), which reads as a soft landing rather than a cost the reader is left holding.
checks.Fix: Cut the sequence off before or just after touchdown on a single small, unresolved physical detail—Wen's calibration marks going dark, or Teo's crate by the door—rather than narrating the full technical success of the landing, so the last note is one unaccounted-for weight rather than a completed process.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The story front-loads complete, first-pass sense (Teo's jettison math, the vote, the descent) while planting details that resonate only in hindsight — Wen's calibration marks 'still true' in the dark after his shop is stripped, Dagny's insistence that 'I want the question to not exist' paired with her later reveal that she voted for her own reasons rather than Prita's, and Teo's fifty-one kilos motif culminating in the blank relocation field that inverts her whole year of measuring others.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose reads as a self-contained, richly built story with invented terms (Hush, freeboard, jettison quota, Air Tax) that are consistently defined in-line through action and dialogue rather than lore-dump exposition — e.g. 'Freeboard, she called this... Candelaria's freeboard was altitude now' — which is a targeted accessibility addition, not a structural rewrite of the narrative itself.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: Nanites (only fleeting robotic 'Almagre' as automaton/AI, not ambient bodily/matter infrastructure), neuretics (mentioned once as a delivery channel for a letter, with no cognitive-divide stakes), and Schism (never mentioned at all) are essentially absent; the story instead builds its own vivid but parallel apparatus of aerobloc physics, Air Tax, and salvage law that substitutes for the actual five pillars.
checks.Fix: Weave in explicit texture for the Schism as the reason airborne blocs and gray-zone law exist, show neuretics creating a real capability/status divide among residents (not just a message conduit), and depict nanites as literally repairing bodies or shaping matter in daily life rather than relying on a single ambiguous automaton called Almagre.
